research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide: write a narrative brief, not keywords; formula Subject + Action + Location + Composition + Style; name lens/aperture ('shallow depth of field (f/1.8)'), shot size and angle; say what you want, not what you don't ('empty street' not 'no cars'); 9:16 is a native ratio; consistency comes from reference images plus a relationship instruction
https://runware.ai/docs/models/google-nano-banana-2/guides/prompting — Nano Banana 2 is Gemini 3.1 Flash Image: detailed scene description and layered structure work better than tag lists

https://nenobanana.com/blogs/nano-banana-character-consistency-12-prompts-that-actually-work--2026-guide — for multi-panel images, restate the person's invariants (face, hair, shirt) and vary only pose, expression and angle; one-image grids drift and cannot be edited panel by panel afterwards
https://www.weshop.ai/solutions/models/nano-banana-2-1-consistent-character-storyboard — storyboard grids: list each panel's action, then repeat 'same face, same outfit in every panel'
https://neilvn.com/tangents/85mm-best-lens-change-portrait-photography/ — 85mm at f/1.4 to f/1.8 is the classic night street portrait: subject sharp, city lights melt into big creamy discs
https://www.sampleshots.com/flickr-photos/46073789951/ — real night street portraits: 85mm f/1.4, ISO 400-800, lit only by available practicals (neon, street lamps, car lights, shop windows)

https://www.jessops.com/c/advice/our-photography-blog/bokeh — bokeh needs lots of varied small lights far behind the subject and a wide aperture with close focus; distance ratio is what makes the discs big

https://expertphotography.com/how-to-clone-yourself-in-photoshop — multiplicity/clone photos: locked tripod, fixed manual exposure and light, one frame per pose, masked together; the lock is what sells 'same moment, same place'
https://www.uniquephoto.com/community/qa/how-were-same-person-twice-photos-made-on-film-cameras — film-era version: half-mask over the lens and double exposure, a hard split line down the frame
https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/split-diopter-lens/ — split diopter: two focal planes in one frame divided by a soft seam (Jaws, De Palma); a visible line that divides one shot into two realities

https://nofilmschool.com/2013/10/deep-focus-use-of-split-diopters-in-film — split diopters and split screens make the audience read two things at once; the dividing seam itself becomes part of the image
attach_reference: yes — attach it as a STYLE reference only (with a line such as 'use the attached photo only for its night colour, bokeh and blacks, not its cars or layout'): a photo carries the exact amber/red/pink/cyan bokeh and inky blacks far better than words. Each prompt also describes the look in full, so it still works if attaching makes the model copy the two taxis' composition; in that case drop the attachment.
notes: Build the final split in the edit, not in one image. One-image grids drift (the lad's face changes from panel to panel) and cannot be edited per panel, and shot C needs the dividing lines as separate layers that a gloved hand can grab and squeeze together; drawn-in lines cannot move. Recommended: generate one hero still of the lad (prompt 1's single-strip framing), then 4-6 single stills of him in each mood with that hero still attached as the character reference and the same camera position (the multiplicity rule: locked camera, same light), and lay them as strips in Premiere with real thin steel-grey line graphics on top, plus a slight glint. Use these three one-image prompts as the look target and as a fallback if the generated grid happens to hold his face. Only the TAXI roof sign may carry readable text; check pub windows for stray lettering.

prompts.idea: Five tall vertical strips, eye-level medium shot on 85mm: the classic clone-photo line-up, the most instant read of 'parallel versions', strips like doors he could step through.
prompts.prompt: A vertical 9:16 night photograph divided into five tall vertical strips by thin, straight, polished steel rods that catch glints of amber streetlight. In every strip stands the same young man with the same face: early twenties, short dark hair, untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and a bit sweaty, a lanyard of car keys in one hand, outside a pub on one city street. Strip by strip he is laughing, swaying, frowning with worry, holding the keys up proudly, reaching for a car door. Medium shot at chest height, 85mm lens at f/1.4, his face sharp, the background melting into large soft bokeh circles of amber, red, pink and cyan. Deep inky blacks, lit only by shop windows, street lamps and a glowing TAXI roof sign. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Six-pane grid seen through a pub window, closer and slightly low: the dividing lines are physical glazing bars, so a hand can believably grab them; closer faces make the moods land on a phone.
prompts.prompt: A vertical 9:16 night photograph split into a grid of six panes, two across and three down, by thin straight black metal glazing bars, like an old window frame between camera and street. Each pane holds a head-and-shoulders portrait of the same young man with the same face: early twenties, short dark hair, untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and sweaty, a lanyard of car keys in one hand. In each pane he wears a different look: grinning, eyes closed mid-sway, worried, smug, wincing, staring at the keys. Slightly low angle, 85mm lens at f/1.8, faces crisp, warm amber pub light on one cheek, the city behind dissolving into big soft bokeh of amber, red, pink and cyan above deep inky blacks, a glowing TAXI roof sign blurred in the background. Thanks.

prompts.idea: A fan of wedges radiating from his raised keys, wider and low on 35mm: the versions literally split off from the moment of decision, and the taut silver wires look grabbable for the squeeze in shot C.
prompts.prompt: A vertical 9:16 night photograph, low angle on a 35mm lens at f/2, of the same young man repeated in five wedge-shaped slices that fan out from his raised fist of car keys at the bottom centre, separated by thin taut silver wires stretched straight from that point to the frame's edges. He is always the same person with the same face: early twenties, short dark hair, untucked white going-out shirt, flushed and a bit sweaty. In each wedge he drifts a little further: arm round a mate, swaying, worried glance back, opening a silver car door, slumped against a lamp post. Wet pavement outside a pub, a blurred taxi with a glowing TAXI roof sign behind, background melting into soft amber, red, pink and cyan bokeh, deep inky blacks. Thanks.
